comments.content: `method` is typed as a free-form `string` while the JSDoc restricts it to `"shell_integration" | "clipboard" | "none"`. This allows arbitrary/typo'd values to leak into telemetry, making aggregation unreliable, and the docs can silently drift from the actual call sites. The rest of this file already uses narrow literal unions for such domains (e.g. `source: "user" | "assistant"` in `captureConversationTurnEvent`); please use the same pattern here.

comments.content: All four new terminal capture methods emit `task.*` events but none of them accept a task identifier, unlike every other task-scoped capture method in this file (`captureTaskCreated`, `captureToolUsage`, `captureTaskInitialization`, etc. all take `ulid`). As a result these events can't be correlated back to a task/session, which is exactly what would be needed to investigate a hang or repeated fallback. The call sites in `src/core/task/index.ts` already have `this.ulid` available, so the identifier should be threaded through all four methods.

comments.content: `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` already calls `getLatestTerminalOutput()` internally (line 30), so this second call re-runs the expensive select-all/copy/restore-clipboard flow. More importantly, unlike the call inside `returnCurrentTerminalContents` (which is wrapped in try/catch), this one is unguarded: `getLatestTerminalOutput()` awaits `vscode.commands.executeCommand(...)`/clipboard reads and can reject, which would escape `run()` before `this.emit("completed")`/`this.emit("continue")` are reached and leave the task hanging. Better to have `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` return the snapshot and reuse it here.

`fullOutput.trim()` being empty only means the command produced no stdout through shell integration (very common for commands like `cd`, `mkdir`, `git add`, `export`), it does not imply a timeout occurred. Overloading `TerminalOutputFailureReason.TIMEOUT` here produces misleading failure telemetry for perfectly normal silent commands. Consider a dedicated reason such as `EMPTY_OUTPUT`/`SHELL_INTEGRATION_NO_OUTPUT` instead.

Same issue as the shell-integration branch: `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` already fetched the snapshot, so calling `getLatestTerminalOutput()` again is redundant. This second call is also not wrapped in try/catch, so a rejection from the terminal/clipboard commands would propagate out of `run()` and skip the `this.emit("completed")`/`this.emit("continue")` emissions below. Return the snapshot from `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` and reuse it (or guard the call).

comments.content: This `catch` handles *all* errors from `this.ask(...)`, but `ask()` also throws expected control-flow errors such as `"Current ask promise was ignored"` (when a newer message supersedes this ask) and `"Cline instance aborted"`. Those are not stream timeouts, so reporting `STREAM_TIMEOUT` here will emit false-positive hang telemetry. Consider checking the error and only capturing when it actually indicates a timeout (or use a distinct stage).

`flushBuffer` sets this timer right before `await this.ask("command_output", chunk)`, and `ask()` blocks in a `pWaitFor` loop until the user responds in the webview. Therefore a 30s timer here primarily measures user response latency, not an actual buffer hang — normal user inactivity will trigger `BUFFER_STUCK` false positives. Consider only measuring the truly-stuck condition (e.g., `chunkEnroute` remaining true without a pending user prompt) or excluding time spent awaiting user input.

This timer is a pure wall-clock deadline, so any command that legitimately runs longer than 60s (dev servers, `npm install`, builds, test suites) will emit a `WAITING_FOR_COMPLETION` "hang" event even though the process is healthy and still producing output. That makes the metric dominated by false positives. Consider treating it as a *no-progress* timeout: start/reset the timer on every `line` event instead of fixed-time from command start.

In those cases `completionTimer` (and `bufferStuckTimer`) stay armed, so a bogus `WAITING_FOR_COMPLETION`/`BUFFER_STUCK` hang is reported for a command that actually failed/was aborted, and a 60s timer is leaked. Please clear the timers in a `finally` block around `await process`.

comments.content: `getLatestTerminalOutput()` returns the whole visible terminal buffer, not the output of the command that just ran, so a non-empty snapshot does not mean the command's output was captured. In practice the buffer almost always still contains output from previously executed commands, so commands that legitimately produce no output (`cd`, `mkdir`, `git add`, `export`) will be recorded as `success: true`. Consider not inferring command success from a generic buffer snapshot (e.g. compare the snapshot before/after the command, or record `captureMethod` + a separate `fallbackAttempted` flag instead of a success boolean).
